# The Sudakov–Fernique inequality

**Sudakov–Fernique inequality** (`sudakov_fernique`): if `X ~ N(0, S)` and `Y ~ N(0, T)` are
centered Gaussian vectors of `ℝ^ι` with `E[(X i - X j)²] ≤ E[(Y i - Y j)²]` for all `i, j`, i.e.
`S i i + S j j - 2 S i j ≤ T i i + T j j - 2 T i j`, then `E[max_i X i] ≤ E[max_i Y i]`.

The proof is the Gaussian interpolation method: for the soft-max `F_β = logSumExp β` and
`Z_t = √t X + √(1 - t) Y` with `X, Y` independent, `ψ(t) = E[F_β(Z_t)]` has derivative
`(1/2) E[∑ᵢⱼ (S - T)ᵢⱼ ∂ᵢⱼF_β(Z_t)]` (`hasDerivAt_integral_comp_gaussianInterp`), which is
nonpositive because `∂ᵢⱼF_β = β (δᵢⱼ pᵢ - pᵢ pⱼ)` with `p` the softmax weights
(`sum_mul_fderiv_fderiv_logSumExp_basisFun`), so that `ψ(1) ≤ ψ(0)`; letting `β → ∞` concludes.
Independent copies of `X` and `Y` are realized as the two blocks `√S (g ∘ inl)`, `√T (g ∘ inr)`
of a standard Gaussian vector `g` of `ℝ^{ι ⊕ ι}` (`blockInl`, `blockInr`).

claims.label: Theorem 1 — fixed-design upper bound O((d log(1/δ) + w(𝒳)²)/ε²)
claims.note: Existential form of the paper's statement, with the explicit constant 600 of the blueprint (the paper's 360 is replaced because the rounding is done by a barrier argument); the blueprint's `thm:upper` is the same guarantee for an explicit algorithm (`Maiti2026Power.isPAC_fixedDesignIdentAlg`). Fully proved (no `sorry`): Kiefer–Wolfowitz design, approximate width minimizer, barrier rounding, least squares, Borell–TIS concentration of the difference process, measurable approximate argmax.

claims.label: Theorem 2 — lower bound Ω(d log(1/δ)/ε²) for every (adaptive) algorithm
claims.note: Explicit constant 1/20000 (the blueprint proof gives 1/(11556 + 5760√2)); δ < 1/16, d ≥ 2. Fully proved (no `sorry`): Kiefer–Wolfowitz normalization, two-point baseline bound, composed test with repeated recommendation, mixture divergence bound, Bretagnolle–Huber.

claims.label: Theorem 3 — lower bound Ω(w(𝒳)²/ε²) for non-adaptive fixed designs
claims.note: Explicit constant 1/70, for δ ≤ 1/10 and budget T ≥ 1. Non-adaptive means a deterministic fixed design with an arbitrary (possibly randomized) recommendation kernel. Proved by the Bayesian argument (prior N(0, τ² Σ_T⁻¹) with τ = √2 - 1, orthogonal decomposition instead of the Gaussian posterior mean), with the singular-design case treated separately.

claims.label: Proposition 4 — w(𝒳) ≤ O(d)
claims.note: Proved, as are the companions `gw_le_sqrt_log_ncard` (w(𝒳) ≤ √(2 d log |𝒳|)) and `sqrt_log_le_gw` (w(𝒳) ≥ (1/8)√(d log ⌊d/2⌋), via the Sudakov–Fernique inequality `ProbabilityTheory.sudakov_fernique`).

claims.label: Theorem 5 — a finite set with w(𝒳) ≤ O(√(d log d)) and √(d log |𝒳|) ≥ Ω(d^{3/4})
claims.note: The set is a multi-task set that does not span ℝ^d; the statement is about its intrinsic width (width inside its span, of dimension r ∈ [d/2, d]), with explicit constants.

claims.label: Theorem 6 — adaptive algorithm with budget O(d log((|𝒳|/d)₊/δ)/ε²) on finite sets
claims.note: Existential form; explicit constant 97281 = 1281 + 6·16000 (Median Elimination constant), with the additive `log(4/δ)` form of the blueprint. Fully proved (no `sorry`): the region algorithm (rounded Kiefer–Wolfowitz design, least-squares candidates per region, Median Elimination on the candidates) as a phased algorithm, analyzed phase by phase through the independence of the future noise from the past; the regions are a cover of `𝒳` by `d` subsets of size at most `⌊|𝒳|/d⌋ + 1`.

claims.label: Table 1 — adaptive lower bound Ω((∑ⱼ √dⱼ)²/ε²) for multi-task bandits
claims.note: Companions in the same file: `hypercubePM_lt_budget_of_isPAC`, `hypercube01_lt_budget_of_isPAC` (Ω(d²/ε²) on the hypercubes), `mSet_lt_budget_of_isPAC` (Ω(m(d-m+1)/ε²) on m-sets) and `unitBall_le_budget_of_isPAC` (Ω(d²/ε²) on the unit ball). All five are proved (no `sorry`): the multi-task, hypercube and m-set bounds follow from the two- and three-point Pinsker toolkit of `Maiti2026Power/LeanMachineLearning/TwoPoint.lean`; the unit-ball bound is the Bayesian argument of the blueprint chapter `prereq_bayes` (`Maiti2026Power/MXJ2026/LowerBall.lean`, Gaussian posterior identities via Stein's identity).

claims.label: Theorem 7 — polynomial separation: adaptive upper bound O((kd log(8k/δ) + d²)/ε²)
claims.note: With `blockBallSet_le_budget_of_isFixedDesign_of_isPAC` (non-adaptive lower bound Ω(kd²/ε²)) and `blockBallSet_le_budget_of_isPAC` (Ω(kd log(1/δ)/ε²)) in the same file. Non-adaptive means a deterministic fixed design with an arbitrary recommendation kernel. The two lower bounds are proved (no `sorry`): the adaptive one from Theorem 2 on the block-ball set, the non-adaptive one by projecting the design on the block receiving the fewest rounds (`isPAC_fixedDesignTransport_blockProjBall`) and applying the Bayesian step of Theorem 3 with the width of the unit ball (`le_gwMat_unitBall`). Only the adaptive upper bound `exists_isPAC_blockBallSet` is proved through the seeded block algorithm `Maiti2026Power.BlockParam.alg` (`Maiti2026Power.BlockParam.one_sub_le_seedMeasure_real_output`, `Maiti2026Power.BlockParam.T_le`).

claims.label: Theorem 8 — ℓ₂-norm estimation with O(d log(1/δ)/ε²) samples
claims.note: Existential form; explicit constant 10⁵ and log(4/δ). Proved (no `sorry`): the algorithm is the seeded meta-algorithm `Maiti2026Power.NormEstParam.alg` with the deterministic output `Maiti2026Power.NormEstParam.output` and budget `Maiti2026Power.NormEstParam.T`; its accuracy `1 - 7δ/8` is `Maiti2026Power.NormEstParam.one_sub_le_seedMeasure_real_output` and its budget bound `Maiti2026Power.NormEstParam.T_le`.

claims.scope:
Phase 1 (statements). The headline results of the paper are stated in Lean, each as a `sorry`-ed theorem, over definitions written in library generality:
Theorem 1 (`exists_isFixedDesign_isPAC`, blueprint `cor:upper_exists`/`thm:upper`): existence of a fixed-design (ε,δ)-PAC algorithm with budget ≤ 600 (w(𝒳)² + d log(2/δ))/ε² + 1. Theorem 2 (`le_budget_of_isPAC`, `thm:lower_adaptive`): every (ε,δ)-PAC algorithm, adaptive or not, has budget ≥ d log(1/δ)/(20000 ε²) when δ < 1/16. Theorem 3 (`le_budget_of_isFixedDesign_of_isPAC`, `thm:lower_nonadaptive`): every fixed-design (ε,δ)-PAC algorithm has budget ≥ w(𝒳)²/(70 ε²) when δ ≤ 1/10. Proposition 4 (`gw_le_card`, `gw_le_sqrt_log_ncard`, `sqrt_log_le_gw`): w(𝒳) ≤ d, w(𝒳) ≤ √(2 d log |𝒳|) for finite 𝒳, and w(𝒳) ≥ (1/8) √(d log ⌊d/2⌋) for d ≥ 4. Theorem 5 (`width_separation`, `thm:width_separation`): a finite multi-task set of intrinsic dimension r ∈ [d/2, d] with intrinsic width ≤ 3 √(d log d) while √(d log |𝒳|) ≥ 0.49 d^{3/4}. Theorem 6 (`exists_isPAC_of_finite`, `cor:log_gains_exists`/`thm:log_gains`): on every finite spanning set there is an adaptive (ε,δ)-PAC algorithm with budget ≤ 97281 d (log((|𝒳|/d)₊) + log(4/δ))/ε². Table 1 adaptive lower bounds (`multitaskSet_lt_budget_of_isPAC`, `hypercubePM_lt_budget_of_isPAC`, `hypercube01_lt_budget_of_isPAC`, `mSet_lt_budget_of_isPAC`, `unitBall_le_budget_of_isPAC`): Ω((∑ⱼ √dⱼ)²/ε²), Ω(d²/ε²) (two hypercubes and the unit ball) and Ω(md/ε²) for m-sets, for every (ε,δ)-PAC algorithm with δ below an absolute constant. Theorem 7 (`blockBallSet_le_budget_of_isFixedDesign_of_isPAC`, `blockBallSet_le_budget_of_isPAC`, `exists_isPAC_blockBallSet`; `thm:separation_lower_nonadaptive`, `cor:separation_exists`): on the block-ball set of ℝ^{kd}, non-adaptive algorithms need Ω(kd log(1/δ)/ε² + kd²/ε²) samples while an adaptive one uses O((kd log(8k/δ) + d²)/ε²). Theorem 8 (`exists_isAccurateNormEst`, `cor:norm_estimation_exists`/`thm:norm_estimation`): an (ε,δ)-accurate ℓ₂-norm estimation algorithm on the unit ball with budget ≤ 10⁵ d log(4/δ)/ε².
The upper bounds (Theorems 1, 6, 7, 8) are stated in the paper's existential form ("there exists an algorithm with budget ≤ …"); the blueprint additionally states them for the explicit algorithms of the paper, whose definitions (rounding, G-optimal designs, Median Elimination, the norm-estimation meta-algorithm) belong to phase 2 together with the proofs (the rounding, the G-optimal designs, Median Elimination and the norm-estimation meta-algorithm are now defined and proved correct).
Phase 2 (proofs) has started with the Gaussian-width area: the support function and the Gaussian width of a set for a measure (`Maiti2026Power/Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/SupportFn.lean` and `Maiti2026Power/Mathlib/Probability/GaussianWidth.lean`: Lipschitz, convexity, images, Minkowski sums, integrability, comparison by convolution/covariance domination), transport lemmas and norm moments of `multivariateGaussian` (`Maiti2026Power/Mathlib/Probability/MultivariateGaussian.lean`), Loewner antitonicity of the matrix inverse (`Maiti2026Power/Mathlib/Matrix/LoewnerInv.lean`), and the width-for-a-matrix and design-set lemmas of the model chapter (`Maiti2026Power/MXJ2026/{Width,DesignSet,WidthDesign}.lean`: `lem:width_matrix_wd`, `lem:width_homog`, `lem:width_mono`, `lem:width_iso`, `lem:width_symm`, `lem:width_empirical`, `lem:designset_basic`, `lem:exists_posdef_design`, `lem:gauss_comparison`), all proved.
Second phase-2 area: optimal experimental design (`Maiti2026Power/MXJ2026/OptimalDesign.lean`, with `Maiti2026Power/Mathlib/Matrix/Loewner.lean` and `Maiti2026Power/Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/LocalExtr.lean`): design distributions as finitely supported weights (`IsDesign`, `designMatrix`), Carathéodory for design matrices, the `G`-value and the identity `∑ λ_x xᵀA(λ)⁻¹x = d`, existence and positivity of `D`-optimal designs, and the Kiefer–Wolfowitz theorem (`exists_isGOptimalDesign`: a `G`-optimal design with `xᵀA⁻¹x ≤ d` on `𝒳` and `= d` on the support) with its normalized form used by the lower bounds; on the library side, the Loewner order versus quadratic forms and congruence, the scalar form of the antitonicity of the inverse, square-root identities and the matrix determinant lemma in rank-one form. The log-det derivative of the blueprint outline was replaced by this rank-one determinant formula (`lem:det_rank_one_mix`). Third area: the rounding theorem (`Maiti2026Power/MXJ2026/Rounding.lean`, `exists_rounding`): for `T ≥ 4d`, every design distribution with positive definite design matrix `A` can be rounded to `T` points of its support with `∑ x xᵀ ⪰ (T/4) A`, by the one-sided barrier argument of Batson–Spielman–Srivastava (barrier potential `tr (B - l I)⁻¹`, Sherman–Morrison, an averaging inequality on eigenvalues), with the consequences on the inverse and on the width of the rounded design; on the library side, traces and inverses of functions of a symmetric matrix through the continuous functional calculus (`Maiti2026Power/Mathlib/Matrix/HermitianCFC.lean`) and the Sherman–Morrison formula. Fourth area: the information-theoretic prerequisites (`Maiti2026Power/Mathlib/InformationTheory/{Pinsker,BretagnolleHuber}.lean`, `Maiti2026Power/Mathlib/Probability/KLGaussian.lean`, `Maiti2026Power/LeanMachineLearning/{DivergenceDecomposition,FixedBudget}.lean`, and — since the LML bump of 2026-09-10 — `LeanMachineLearning/ForMathlib/InformationTheory/KullbackLeibler/` and `LeanMachineLearning/SequentialLearning/DivergenceDecomposition.lean`): the integrated chain rule `klDiv (μ ⊗ₘ κ) (ν ⊗ₘ η) = klDiv μ ν + ∫⁻ klDiv (κ a) (η a) ∂μ` (with the measurability of `a ↦ klDiv (κ a) (η a)`), the divergence of two Gaussians, Pinsker's and the Bretagnolle–Huber inequalities, the divergence decomposition for an algorithm run against two stationary environments (`IsAlgEnvSeq.klDiv_map_history`) with its linear Gaussian form, and the data-processing step for the outputs of fixed-budget runs (the stopping time of a fixed-budget algorithm is constant; the divergence of the output laws is bounded by `T R² ‖θ - θ'‖² / 2`, and Bretagnolle–Huber bounds the sum of the error probabilities of any test on the output). The output kernels of an identification algorithm are now required to be s-finite (`IdentAlg.isSFiniteKernel_output`). Fifth area: existence and transport of runs (`Maiti2026Power/LeanMachineLearning/Run.lean`: the canonical run of a fixed-budget algorithm on the space of (trajectory, output) pairs, `IsFixedBudget.isRun_fixedBudgetRunMeasure`; runs transported along maps of the sample space), the geometry of the normalized `G`-optimal design (`Maiti2026Power/MXJ2026/NormalizedDesign.lean`: `∑ λ_x ⟪v₁, v_x⟫² = 1/d` and a well-separated pair of unit arms), convexity of the divergence in its second argument (`LeanMachineLearning/ForMathlib/InformationTheory/KullbackLeibler/Convex.lean`, upstreamed on 2026-09-10), and the **baseline adaptive lower bound** `T ≥ (2 - √2)/(32 ε²) log(1/(4δ))` for `(ε, δ)`-PAC fixed-budget algorithms on spanning sets in dimension `d ≥ 2`, `δ < 1/4` (`Maiti2026Power/MXJ2026/LowerAdaptiveBaseline.lean`, `baseline_le_budget_of_isPAC`, blueprint `lem:baseline_lower`) — the two-point half of Theorem 2, proved in the original coordinates (no transformation of the algorithm). Because runs can only be constructed in the universe of the action set, `LinearBandit.IsPAC` now quantifies over probability spaces in the universe of the ambient space `E` (it was universe-polymorphic); the comparator challenges were regenerated accordingly. Sixth area: the noise of linear Gaussian runs (`Maiti2026Power/LeanMachineLearning/GaussianNoise.lean`): conditionally on the history and the current action, `Y_t - ⟪X_t, θ⟫` has the law `N(0,1)` (the blueprint's noise representation), hence is conditionally sub-Gaussian, and Mathlib's Azuma–Hoeffding inequality bounds the noise sums of any block of rounds (`IsAlgEnvSeq.measureReal_abs_sum_noise_ge_le`), which is the concentration input of the estimation phase of Theorem 2's mixture test. Seventh area: **Theorem 2 is proved** (`le_budget_of_isPAC`, no `sorry`). The missing pieces were the composed test and its analysis: algorithms agreeing on a prefix and the transfer of a PAC guarantee to a partial run (`Maiti2026Power/LeanMachineLearning/AlgorithmPrefix.lean`), the algorithm `Algorithm.thenRepeat` "play `alg`, then repeat an action drawn from a kernel" and the test algorithm `IdentAlg.testAlg` built from an identification algorithm (`RepeatTest.lean`), the error bounds of the test in a linear Gaussian bandit via the Azuma bound of the sixth area (`RepeatTestGaussian.lean`), and the mixture testing problem (`Maiti2026Power/MXJ2026/MixtureKL.lean`: the divergence from the null law of histories to the design-weighted mixture of the alternatives is at most `(N+1)·9ε²/(2d)`, and the Bretagnolle–Huber inequality for this mixture). The blueprint's general sequential composition lemma (`lem:composition`) is not formalized; the new `lem:prefix_transfer` is the special case that is needed. Eighth area (towards Theorem 1): fixed-design runs and least squares. A sequence whose conditional law given its past is constant is i.i.d. (`Maiti2026Power/Mathlib/Probability/IidOfCondDistrib.lean`), hence the noise of any linear Gaussian run is an i.i.d. `N(0,1)` vector (standard Gaussian on `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin T)`), and under a fixed design the observation vector is `Xθ` plus this noise (`Maiti2026Power/LeanMachineLearning/FixedDesignRun.lean`, blueprint `lem:fixed_design_law`); the least-squares estimator `Σ⁻¹ Xᵀ y` has the law `N(θ, Σ⁻¹)` (`Maiti2026Power/MXJ2026/LeastSquares.lean`, `lem:least_squares_law`). Also the mixed design `½ λ₁ + ½ λ_G` with its `G`-optimality and width bounds (`MixedDesign.lean`), the regret bound by the difference process (`DifferenceProcess.lean`) and a measurable `γ`-approximate argmax selector on a compact set (`Maiti2026Power/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/ApproxArgmax.lean`). What remains for Theorem 1 is the Borell–TIS inequality (Gaussian concentration chapter), the attainment of the width and the assembly of the algorithm. Ninth area: **Gaussian concentration** (blueprint chapter `prereq_concentration`, previously entirely unformalized; Mathlib has no Gaussian concentration inequality). `Maiti2026Power/Mathlib/Probability/GaussianMGF.lean` (MGF of a linear form under the standard Gaussian, exponential moments of Gaussian norms from Fernique), `MaureyPisier.lean` (the Maurey–Pisier argument: a `C¹` function with `‖∇f‖ ≤ L` has a sub-Gaussian MGF with constant `c_G L²`, `c_G = π²/4`, via quarter-circle interpolation, Jensen, Fubini and Mathlib's rotation invariance of `μ ⊗ μ`), `Maiti2026Power/Mathlib/Analysis/{SpecialFunctions,InnerProductSpace}/LogSumExp.lean` (the log-sum-exp function and softmax weights on `ι → ℝ`, and the log-sum-exp smoothing of a finite maximum of linear forms as their composition with `v ↦ (⟪x i, v⟫)ᵢ`, its gradient), `SupportFnDense.lean` (the support function of a compact set as a supremum over a dense sequence, with monotone partial maxima) and `BorellTIS.lean` (concentration of finite and compact suprema of Gaussian linear forms, the **Borell–TIS inequality** for the standard Gaussian and for `N(0, S)`). Tenth area: **Theorem 1 is proved** (`exists_isFixedDesign_isPAC`, no `sorry`): the difference process and its concentration (`Maiti2026Power/MXJ2026/DifferenceProcess.lean`), the output law of fixed-budget runs (`IsRun.hasCondDistrib_output_finHistory`), the explicit fixed-design algorithm `fixedDesignIdentAlg T x s` (rounded design, least squares, measurable approximate argmax) with its guarantee `isPAC_fixedDesignIdentAlg` in the general form of the blueprint's `thm:upper` (`Maiti2026Power/MXJ2026/FixedDesignAlgorithm.lean`), and the assembly with the Kiefer–Wolfowitz design, an approximate width minimizer, the mixed design, the barrier rounding and the arithmetic of the constant 600 (`Maiti2026Power/MXJ2026/Upper.lean`). Eleventh area: **the Gaussian width chapter, upper bounds and Theorem 5**. `Maiti2026Power/Mathlib/Probability/SubgaussianMax.lean` (expected maximum of finitely many sub-Gaussian variables, `E[max_i Z_i] ≤ √(2 c log m)`, and the Gaussian width of a finite set), `Maiti2026Power/MXJ2026/WidthUpper.lean` (Proposition 4 (i)/(ii) for the `G`-optimal design matrix, the regionalized width and its bound `√(2 d log p)`), `Maiti2026Power/MXJ2026/IntrinsicWidth.lean` (a basis-free reduction: the intrinsic width of a non-spanning set is at most `E sup_{x ∈ 𝒳} ⟪x, G⟫` for a Gaussian vector `G` on the span whose covariance is the pseudo-inverse of a design matrix) and `Maiti2026Power/MXJ2026/Multitask.lean` (the multi-task set: one-hot parametrization, cardinality, support function as a sum of block maxima, span = vectors with equal block sums and its dimension `∑ d_j - m + 1`, the uniform design and its pseudo-inverse, and `intrinsicGw_multitaskSet_le : w_int(𝒳) ≤ ∑ √(2 d_j log d_j)`). **Theorem 5 is proved** (`width_separation`, no `sorry`), as are `gw_le_card` and `gw_le_sqrt_log_ncard` (Proposition 4 (i), (ii)). Twelfth area: **the Sudakov–Fernique chapter and Proposition 4 (iii)**. `Maiti2026Power/Mathlib/Probability/SteinReal.lean` (Stein's identity `E[(ξ - μ) f(ξ)] = v E[f'(ξ)]` for `N(μ, v)`), `SteinIdentity.lean` (Stein's identity for the standard Gaussian measure of a finite-dimensional inner product space, `E[⟪a, g⟫ F(g)] = E[DF(g) a]`, for `N(0, S)`, `E[⟪a, X⟫ F(X)] = E[DF(X) (S a)]`, and for linear images, by Fubini along an orthonormal basis), `GaussianInterpolation.lean` (the interpolation `√t L₁ + √(1 - t) L₀` and the **Gaussian interpolation formula**: derivative of `E[F(Z_t)]` under the integral sign plus Stein), `SudakovFernique.lean` (the **Sudakov–Fernique inequality** `E[max_i X_i] ≤ E[max_i Y_i]` for centered Gaussian vectors with `E[(X_i - X_j)²] ≤ E[(Y_i - Y_j)²]`, via the soft-max and independent blocks on `ℝ^{ι ⊕ ι}`), `GaussianMaxLower.lean` (lower Mills ratio, `E[ξ⁺] = (2π)^{-1/2}`, `E[max(ξ₁, ξ₂)] = π^{-1/2}`, and `E[max_{i ≤ m} ξ_i] ≥ √(log m) / 4` for i.i.d. standard Gaussians, `m ≥ 2`), `Maiti2026Power/Mathlib/Analysis/{SpecialFunctions,InnerProductSpace}/LogSumExp.lean` (Hessian of the log-sum-exp and its operator-norm bound), `Maiti2026Power/Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/IsotropicSeparated.lean` (a weighted family in isotropic position has `m` points pairwise `√(d + 1 - m)`-separated), and `Maiti2026Power/MXJ2026/WidthLower.lean` (the whitened design is isotropic; Sudakov minoration `gwMat 𝒳 A ≥ √(d log ⌊d/2⌋) / 8`). **Proposition 4 is now fully proved** (`sqrt_log_le_gw`, no `sorry`).
Thirteenth area: **Theorem 3 is proved** (`le_budget_of_isFixedDesign_of_isPAC`, no `sorry`), by the Bayesian argument of the paper. New library files: `Maiti2026Power/Mathlib/Probability/StdGaussianProd.lean` (the product of two standard Gaussian measures is Gaussian; covariance of linear forms of an independent pair; **independence of uncorrelated linear images** `indepFun_add_prod_stdGaussian_of_comp_adjoint_eq_zero`), `Maiti2026Power/Mathlib/Probability/IndepIntegral.lean` (`E⟪f(V), W⟫ = 0` for `W` centered and independent of `V`, `f` bounded), `Maiti2026Power/Mathlib/Probability/Kernel/PriorAverage.lean` (the expected loss of a procedure that fails with probability `≤ δ` under every parameter is at most `ε + δ ∫ Z dπ`), and additions to `Maiti2026Power/Mathlib/Probability/CondDistrib.lean` (transport of `μ ⊗ₘ κ.comap f`). New project files: `Maiti2026Power/LeanMachineLearning/FixedDesignLaw.lean` (the explicit law `fixedDesignPairLaw A x θ` of (history, output) of a fixed-design fixed-budget run, and the PAC property on that law), `Maiti2026Power/MXJ2026/SingularDesign.lean` (a singular design leaves a direction invisible; two reward vectors with equal means whose regrets sum to `4 ε`) and `Maiti2026Power/MXJ2026/BayesModel.lean` (the Bayesian model on a standard Gaussian pair `(g, η)`: prior `θ = τ Σ_T^{-1/2} g`, observations, history and recommendation kernel; the orthogonal decomposition `θ = W + c Σ_T⁻¹ Xᵀ y` with `W` independent of `y`; the Bayes identity `E⟪rec, θ⟫ = c E⟪rec, Σ_T⁻¹ Xᵀ y⟫`; the lower bound `E[r] ≥ τ w_T - c (τ w_T + w_T)` and the PAC upper bound `E[r] ≤ ε + 2 τ δ w_T`).
Fourteenth area: **four of the five adaptive lower bounds of Table 1 are proved** (`multitaskSet_lt_budget_of_isPAC`, `hypercubePM_lt_budget_of_isPAC`, `hypercube01_lt_budget_of_isPAC`, `mSet_lt_budget_of_isPAC`, no `sorry`; only the unit ball, which needs the Gaussian-prior chapter `prereq_bayes`, is left). The shared toolkit is `Maiti2026Power/LeanMachineLearning/TwoPoint.lean`: the divergence between the laws of the outputs of two runs of a fixed-budget algorithm is at most the expected sum of the squared gaps along the trajectory (`IsRun.klDiv_map_out_le_sum_integral`, data processing on top of the divergence decomposition), hence the **two-point inequality** `|P_θ(E) - P_θ'(E)| ≤ √(K/2)` for any bound `K` on that divergence (`IsRun.abs_measureReal_sub_le_of_sum_le`, with the uniform-bound special case `..._of_sq_le`), the **three-point inequality** `P_{θ⁺}(E) + P_{θ⁻}(Eᶜ) ≥ 1 - 2√(TC/4)` (`IsRun.one_sub_le_measureReal_add_of_sq_le`) and the conversion of a PAC guarantee into an expected-regret bound `E[r] ≤ ε + (Z - ε) δ` (`integral_simpleRegret_le_of_measureReal_le`). On the combinatorial side, `Fintype.sum_sum_update` (summing over all values of one coordinate of a dependent product multiplies the sum by the cardinality of that coordinate, via an involution) and `Finset.sum_powersetCard_succ_sum_mem` (the pairs `(S, i)` with `|S| = k+1`, `i ∈ S`, are in bijection with the pairs `(B, i)` with `|B| = k`, `i ∉ B`). The two hypercubes are handled at once as vertex sets of a box with two values per coordinate (`Maiti2026Power/MXJ2026/CubeSet.lean`: support function of a box, simple regret as a Hamming distance; `LowerCube.lean`: `le_of_isPAC_cubeSet`, blueprint `def:cube_set`, `lem:lower_cube`); the multi-task instances and their lower bound are in `MultitaskInstances.lean` and `LowerMultitask.lean`, the `m`-set ones in `MSetInstances.lean` and `LowerMSet.lean`.
Fifteenth area: **Theorem 6 is proved** (`exists_isPAC_of_finite`, no `sorry`), through a reusable framework of **phased algorithms** (`Maiti2026Power/LeanMachineLearning/Phased.lean`, `PhasedAlg`: deterministic algorithms which run in phases of fixed lengths, play in each phase a fixed design determined by a state and update the state from the observations of the phase; `PhasedAlg.toAlgorithm`, `PhasedAlg.toIdentAlg`, `PhasedAlg.cons`). In a linear Gaussian bandit the noise of a phase is i.i.d. `N(0,1)` and independent of the state at the start of the phase (`hasCondDistrib_phaseNoise`, from the new library lemmas `hasCondDistrib_pi_of_hasCondDistrib_const` — a sequence whose conditional law given an extra variable and its past is constant is i.i.d. and independent of that variable — and `IsAlgEnvSeq.hasCondDistrib_noise_window`), which gives a phase-by-phase union bound (`one_sub_sum_le_measureReal_stateProc_mem`, via the Fubini bound `HasCondDistrib.measureReal_sub_le`) and PAC guarantees (`isPAC_toIdentAlg`); this replaces the blueprint's sequential composition of algorithms (`lem:composition`, still not formalized) for this class. **Median Elimination** (`MedianEliminationSchedule.lean`: the schedule `ε_ℓ, δ_ℓ, n_ℓ`, the halving sizes `s_ℓ`, the number of rounds and the budget `N_ME ≤ 16000 K log(3/δ)/ε²`; `MedianEliminationRound.lean`: the round-robin design of a round, empirical means, top-`⌈s/2⌉` selection through the new `Maiti2026Power/Mathlib/Data/Finset/TopBy.lean` (`Finset.topBy`, its cardinality, the comparison property, the median counting argument and its measurability in the scores), the sub-Gaussian tails of the empirical means and the one-round guarantee `lem:me_round`; `MedianElimination.lean`: the phased algorithm on candidate arms, the good surviving sets and `isPAC_medianElim`, blueprint `thm:median_elimination`/`cor:median_elimination_linear`, formalized for Gaussian rewards of candidate arms of a linear bandit rather than general sub-Gaussian bandits). The **region algorithm** (`Maiti2026Power/MXJ2026/RegionAlgorithm.lean`: a fixed-design phase computing least-squares candidates in the regions, prepended to Median Elimination with parameters `(ε/2, δ/2)`; the first-phase guarantee `lem:region_phase1` by Borell–TIS on the region of an optimal arm; `isPAC_regionAlg`, blueprint `thm:log_gains`) and the assembly in `LogGains.lean` (a cover of `𝒳` by `d` regions of size at most `⌊|𝒳|/d⌋ + 1`, `Maiti2026Power/Mathlib/Data/Set/CoverSmall.lean`; Kiefer–Wolfowitz design, barrier rounding, `T₁ = ⌈640 (w_𝓡² + d log(4/δ))/ε²⌉`, and the budget arithmetic `Maiti2026Power/MXJ2026/LogGainsArith.lean` giving the constant `97281 = 1281 + 6·16000`).
Sixteenth area: **the two lower bounds of Theorem 7 are proved** (`blockBallSet_le_budget_of_isFixedDesign_of_isPAC`, `blockBallSet_le_budget_of_isPAC`, no `sorry`). The adaptive bound is Theorem 2 on the block-ball set, which is compact and spanning (`Maiti2026Power/MXJ2026/BlockBall.lean`: block embeddings and projections, support function `max_i ‖θ⁽ⁱ⁾‖`, regret identity for reward vectors supported on one block). The non-adaptive bound follows the blueprint's block restriction, in the form of a **transport lemma** (`Maiti2026Power/LeanMachineLearning/FixedDesignTransport.lean`: a fixed-design PAC algorithm on `𝒳 ⊆ E` transported through a linear map `L : F → E` to a design on `𝒴 ⊆ F` with the same observation laws and a regret-non-increasing recommendation map is PAC on `𝒴`, `isPAC_fixedDesignTransport`, proved on the explicit laws `fixedDesignPairLaw`): the design projected on the block receiving the fewest rounds (pigeonhole) is PAC on the unit ball of `ℝ^d`. Theorem 3's proof was split into reusable lemmas (positive definiteness of a PAC design, `posDef_of_isFixedDesign_of_isPAC*`, now also for budget `0` on sets containing `0`; the Bayesian step `gwMat_le_of_isFixedDesign_of_isPAC`, `0.12 w(𝒳, Σ_T) ≤ ε`), and the width of the unit ball for a matrix is bounded below (`Maiti2026Power/MXJ2026/WidthBall.lean`: `gwMat (unitBall) A ≥ √(2/π) d / √(tr A)`, from `E‖Y‖ ≥ √(2/π) ∑ cᵢ √(Sᵢᵢ)` for `Y ~ N(0, S)` and unit weights `c`, `Maiti2026Power/Mathlib/Probability/GaussianAbsMoment.lean`, with `E|Z| = √(2v/π)` for `Z ~ N(0, v)`; blueprint `prop:width_ball`, sharpened from `d/√3` to `√(2/π) d`), with `tr Σ' ≤ T/k`.
Seventeenth area: **the unit-ball lower bound of Table 1 is proved** (`unitBall_le_budget_of_isPAC`, no `sorry`), completing Table 1, through the Bayesian analysis of adaptive algorithms of the blueprint chapter `prereq_bayes`. Library: `Maiti2026Power/LeanMachineLearning/EnvDensity.lean` (the **environment likelihood ratio**: for reward kernels `κ = κ₀.withDensity ρ`, the law of the history of any algorithm under `κ` is the law under `κ₀` with density `∏ ρ (x t) (y t)`, `IsAlgEnvSeq.map_finHistory_eq_withDensity_env`, the environment analogue of LML's `Algorithm.density`, with the kernel-level identity `Kernel.compProd_withDensity_right`), `Maiti2026Power/Mathlib/Probability/GaussianDensityRatio.lean` (`N(m,1) = N(0,1).withDensity (exp (y m - m²/2))`), `Maiti2026Power/Mathlib/Probability/SteinExpGrowth.lean` (**Stein's identity for `C¹` functions of exponential growth**, one-dimensional, standard Gaussian and `N(0, S)`), `Maiti2026Power/Mathlib/Matrix/TraceInv.lean` (AM–HM: `d² ≤ tr A · tr A⁻¹`). Project: `GaussianLikelihood.lean` (the likelihood ratio `exp (∑ (yₜ ⟪xₜ, θ⟫ - ⟪xₜ, θ⟫²/2))` of a linear Gaussian history, jointly measurable), `BayesKernel.lean` (the law of the history under `θ` as a Markov kernel `histKernel` built from the pure-noise law and the likelihood, the pair kernel with the recommendation, and the PAC property on it — this sidesteps the measurability of `θ ↦ trajMeasure`), `PosteriorGaussian.lean` (**Gaussian posterior identities via Stein**: for the tilt `ℓ(θ) = exp(⟪b,θ⟫ - θᵀSθ/2)` of `N(0, σ²I)`, `∫ (θ - m) ℓ dπ = 0` and `∫ ‖θ - m‖² ℓ dπ = tr V ∫ ℓ dπ` with `V = (σ⁻²I + S)⁻¹`, `m = V b`; no Lebesgue density or completion of the square), `LowerBall.lean` (the joint law `(π ⊗ Q₀).withDensity ℓ`, Fubini, the Cauchy–Schwarz bound `E⟪rec, θ⟫ ≤ √(σ²d - d²/(dσ⁻² + T))`, `E‖θ‖ ≥ √(2/π) σ √d`, the Bayesian regret bound, truncation of the prior, existence of a hard instance with `‖θ‖ ≤ 10d/√T` and `E_θ[r] ≥ 3d/(40√T)`, the budget-0 case). The headline proof in `LogGains.lean` is the final arithmetic with `δ ≤ 1/500`.
Eighteenth area (2026-09-06): **sub-exponential random variables**, the blueprint chapter `prereq_subexp`, first prerequisite of Theorem 8 (all its statements are now formalized except the unused Gaussian quadratic-form lemma). Library: `Maiti2026Power/Mathlib/Probability/Moments/SubExponential.lean` (the structure `HasSubexponentialMGF X V b μ` with real parameters and the range `b * |t| ≤ 1` of `t`, so that `b = 0` is Mathlib's `HasSubgaussianMGF`; integrability of all moments and centering via the derivative of the MGF at `0` and Fermat's rule; scaling, transport along maps, independent sums; the **Bernstein tail bounds** `exp (-min (t²/(2V)) (t/(2b)))`, one- and two-sided, and for averages of independent variables), `Maiti2026Power/Mathlib/Probability/GaussianSquareMGF.lean` (the Gaussian integral of a quadratic exponent, `E[exp (a X²)] = (1 - 2va)^(-1/2) exp (m² a / (1 - 2va))` for `X ~ N(m, v)`, the centered square of a Gaussian has parameters `(8 (v² + m² v), 4v)`, **chi-square**: `‖g‖² - d` has parameters `(8d, 4)` under `stdGaussian`, with the tails `P(‖g‖² - d ≥ t) ≤ exp (-min (t²/(16d)) (t/8))` and `P(‖g‖² ≥ 2d + 12 log(1/δ)) ≤ δ`; `exp x ≤ 1 + x + x²/2` for `x ≤ 0`), `Maiti2026Power/Mathlib/Probability/SubgaussianSquare.lean` (the **Gaussian trick** `E[exp (a Z²)] ≤ (1 - 2ca)^(-1/2)` for a sub-Gaussian `Z` by Tonelli on `μ.prod N(0,1)`, the fourth moment `E[Z⁴] ≤ 14 c²`, and the general statement: if `Z` is sub-Gaussian with constant `c` and `E[Z²] = c` then `Z² - c` has parameters `(16c², 4c)`), `Maiti2026Power/Mathlib/Probability/Rademacher.lean` (`signMeasure`, `rademacherMeasure ι` as a product measure, independence and moments of the coordinates, Hoeffding coordinatewise so that `∑ εᵢ θᵢ` is sub-Gaussian with constant `‖θ‖²`, its second moment `‖θ‖²`, and the centered square with parameters `(16‖θ‖⁴, 4‖θ‖²)`, which replaces the paper's Hanson–Wright step). The exact Rademacher fourth moment of the blueprint was replaced by the sub-Gaussian bound `14c²`, which suffices.
Nineteenth area (2026-09-06): **seeded algorithms and the seed representation of runs** (blueprint `lem:seeded` in the model chapter), the LML-side tool used to prove PAC guarantees of adaptive algorithms without conditional-expectation arguments. `Maiti2026Power/Mathlib/Probability/CondDistribConst.lean` (the kernel `Kernel.mapOfConst Q G` mapping `x` to the law of `G x e`, `e ~ Q`; conditional distributions of functions of a variable and an independent noise) and `Maiti2026Power/LeanMachineLearning/Seeded.lean` (the structure `SeededAlg` — a seed law, a first action and measurable next-action maps —, its `Algorithm`, noise environments `noiseEnv μe F` with `linearGaussianEnv = noiseEnv`, the recursively defined run `seedStep` on the product space `seedMeasure = (seed ⊗ μe)^ℕ`, which is an `IsAlgEnvSeq`; uniqueness of the law of the history of an `IsAlgEnvSeq` (`IsAlgEnvSeq.map_history_eq`), hence every run of a seeded algorithm in a noise environment has the law of the seed run; the PAC guarantee `linearBandit_isPAC_fixedBudget_deterministic` of a fixed-budget seeded algorithm with a deterministic output from a bound on the seed space, universe-polymorphic in the sample space).
Twentieth area (2026-09-06): **Theorem 8 is proved** (`exists_isAccurateNormEst`, no `sorry`), the whole norm-estimation chapter (`norm_estimation.tex`) being formalized and tagged. Statistics on product spaces: `RademacherStat.lean` (Rademacher directions `radDir` from Boolean seeds, the block space `rbMeasure ι s K`, the squared statistic `rbStat` and its decomposition into Term 1 `rbX` (sub-exponential `(16‖θ‖⁴, 4‖θ‖²)`, independent) and Term 2 `rbW` (conditionally sub-exponential given the directions, Fubini over the directions), the variance-proxy bound `rbMeasure_real_rbVbar_gt_le`), `RademacherEst.lean` (Algorithm 1: `rbMeasure_real_sqrt_addEst_gt_le`, accuracy `ε/2` with failure `3δ/8` when `‖θ‖/2 < r₀ ≤ 2‖θ‖`), `RademacherTest.lean` (the scale tests `rbMeasure_real_test_h0_le`/`h1_le`, error `3δ'/4`), `LargeNormStat.lean` (the basis-design estimator `lnEst` on the noise space `lnNoise`, `lnNoise_real_lnEst_gt_le`, failure `δ/2` when `√d ≤ ‖θ‖`, using `GaussianSum.lean`: sums of independent Gaussians are Gaussian). The meta-algorithm: `NormEstParams.lean`/`NormEstSchedule.lean` (scales `t_j = 2^j ε`, `δ_j = δ/2^(j+2)`, `J`, the phase starts, the round schedule `rbBlock`/`basisRound` of the two phases), `NormEstStat.lean` (window statistics of an observation sequence, the first-phase outcome `jStar` and the estimate, all measurable), `NormEstAlg.lean` (the seeded algorithm `NormEstParam.alg` with uniform Boolean seeds and its deterministic output), `NormEstWindows.lean` + `Maiti2026Power/Mathlib/Probability/InfinitePiWindow.lean` (the seed space `nsMeasure`, the window projections `rbProj`/`lnProj` whose laws are the block and noise laws, and their independence from the prefix of the seed sequence — coordinates of an i.i.d. sequence indexed by an injective family are i.i.d.), `NormEstPlan.lean` (the run follows the plan: `seedAction_eq_planAction` by strong induction on the rounds, and the identification of the window statistics of the run with `rbStat`/`lnR` of the window projections), `NormEstProof.lean` (the good event of the multi-scale phase, `3δ/8`; the trichotomy `jStar_bounds` on the outcome; the failure of the second phase at outcome `j` is independent of `{jStar = j}`, total failure `7δ/8`), `NormEstBudget.lean` (the budget `T ≤ 10⁵ d log(4/δ)/ε²` with `T₁ ≤ 63736 dL/ε²` and `N₂ ≤ 32776 dL/ε²`). Deviations from the paper are recorded in the blueprint chapter: all tests of the multi-scale phase are run (the ones after the stopping scale are ignored), the phases are composed by a deterministic round schedule on the seed space instead of sequential composition, and the large-norm regime uses the basis design.
Twenty-first area (2026-09-06): **Theorem 7's adaptive upper bound is proved** (`exists_isPAC_blockBallSet`, no `sorry`), which completes phase 2: every headline statement of the paper is now proved. The block algorithm (`BlockAlg.lean`) is a seeded algorithm with the seeds of the meta-algorithm: in phase 1 the rounds `[iN, (i+1)N)` run the norm estimator `NormEst(ε/4, δ/(2k))` embedded on block `i` (the next-action map applies the block embedding to the next-action map of the meta-algorithm evaluated on the projected history of the block); in phase 2 the basis vectors of the block `î` maximizing the estimates are played `n₂` times each and the normalized empirical mean vector is recommended. `BlockPlan.lean` proves by strong induction that the run on each block is the run of the meta-algorithm against `θ^(i)` on the shifted seed sequence (`seedStep_block`), that the phase-2 actions are the basis vectors of `î` (`seedAction_of_T₂_le`) and that the empirical mean vector is `θ^(î) + Δ` with `Δ` the noise average of the basis window (`thetaHat_eq`); the seed measure is shift-invariant (`nsMeasure_map_shiftSeq`, from the identification of `infinitePi` through its cylinders, `InfinitePiWindow.lean`). `BlockProof.lean`: the deterministic regret bound `regret_le` (support function of the block-ball set, `‖ϑ‖ - ⟪v/‖v‖, ϑ⟫ ≤ 2‖v - ϑ‖`), the chi-square tail for `‖Δ‖` on the noise space, the union bound over the blocks (`7δ/16`) plus the phase-2 failure (`δ/2`) — no conditioning on the first phase is needed since the phase-2 failure event only involves the noises of the basis window — and the budget `k N + d n₂ ≤ 2·10⁶ (kd log(8k/δ) + d²)/ε²`.
Twenty-second area (2026-09-07): **the sub-exponential file has feature parity with Mathlib's `SubGaussian.lean`** (new Section `sec:pre_subexp_kernel` of the blueprint, 73 new tagged declarations, nothing used by Part I). `Kernel.HasSubexponentialMGF X V b κ ν` (integrability w.r.t. `κ ∘ₘ ν` for admissible `t`, a.e. mgf bound) with the basic a.e. properties, `of_ae_mgf_le` (the "for all `t`, a.e." to "a.e., for all `t`" upgrade by continuity of the mgf on the interior of the admissible interval plus the two endpoints), stability lemmas, a.e. Bernstein tails, the Hölder sum `add_of_holderConjugate` (parameters `(p VX + q VY, max (p bX) (q bY))`), and `add_compProd`/`add_comp` whose integrability part goes through the Lebesgue integral (Cauchy–Schwarz needs `2t` admissible, so Mathlib's argument does not transfer); `HasCondSubexponentialMGF` via `condExpKernel`; the measure version now derived from the kernel one (tail bounds no longer need a finite measure), with `trim`, `add`, `sub_of_indepFun`, **Bernstein's inequality** for sums (`measure_sum_ge_le_of_iIndepFun` and variants), `measureReal_le_le_exp`, `ae_eq_zero_of_hasSubexponentialMGF_zero` (parameters `(0, b)` force `X = 0` a.s., via Jensen and the second derivative of the mgf); **Bernstein's condition** `hasSubexponentialMGF_of_abs_le_of_integral_eq_zero` (`|X| ≤ M`, centered, `E X² ≤ v` gives `(3v/2, M)`, from `Real.exp_bound`); the martingale lemmas `add_of_hasCondSubexponentialMGF`, `sum_of_hasCondSubexponentialMGF` and the **Azuma–Bernstein inequality** `measure_sum_ge_le_of_hasCondSubexponentialMGF`.
Rename (2026-09-07): the Lean library, package and namespace `COLT83` became `Maiti2026Power` (directory `Maiti2026Power/`, root `Maiti2026Power.lean`); the blueprint tags, the comparator challenges (regenerated with the referee) and CI were updated accordingly. The repository name `colt-2026-83` and its URLs are unchanged.
Twenty-third area (2026-09-13): **the project uses LML's identification algorithms.** LML now defines `Learning.IdentAlg 𝓞 𝓐 𝓨 𝓓` (`SequentialLearning/IdentificationAlg.lean`: a sampling rule, a measurable stopping rule `stopSet` on histories of variable length and a Markov output kernel on histories of variable length), the stopping time `hittingAfter (sigmaHistory O X Y) S 0` and stopped history `stoppedValue` of a stopping rule, the law `stoppedHistMeasure` of the stopped history, runs `IdentAlg.IsRun`, the law of the output `IdentAlg.outputMeasure` and the PAC property `IdentAlg.IsPAC` (a bound on the probability of a *bad* output under that law). The local `IdentAlg` structure, stopping time, stopped history, run and PAC definitions, and the local sigma-type measurability file were deleted in favour of LML's; `Maiti2026Power/LeanMachineLearning/IdentAlg.lean` now only holds fixed budgets and fixed designs (`IsFixedBudget`, `fixedBudget` — its output rule on histories of length `T` is `A.output.comap (Sigma.mk T) _`, `IsFixedDesign`, `fixedDesignAlg`, and the fixed-budget run lemmas), `Run.lean` the transport of runs and the canonical run `IdentAlg.runMeasure` of *every* identification algorithm (which replaces the fixed-budget-only `fixedBudgetRunMeasure`) with the criterion `IsPAC.of_forall_isRun`, and `StoppedHistory.lean`/`DivergenceDecomposition.lean` restate the stopped-history layer and the divergence decomposition at a stopping time on LML's `sigmaHistory`, Mathlib's `hittingAfter`, `stoppedValue` and `stoppedProcess` (the history stopped at time `M`). `LinearBandit.IsPAC 𝒳 A ε δ` is now `A.IsPAC (linearGaussianEnv 𝒳) (fun θ x ↦ ε < simpleRegret 𝒳 θ x) δ`, a statement about the law of the recommendation with no universe parameter, with the run forms `IsPAC.le_measureReal_of_isRun` and `isPAC_of_forall_isRun`; all PAC lemmas were flipped to the badness form (`IsPAC.measureReal_bad_of_isAlgEnvSeqUntil`, `IsPAC.measureReal_bad_action_succ_of_testAlg`, `SeededAlg.isPAC_fixedBudget_deterministic`, `PhasedAlg.isPAC_toIdentAlg`, `IsAccurateNormEst`). The blueprint tags and text, and the comparator challenges (whose vendored LML block now also carries the trajectory measure, `sigmaHistory`, `stoppedHistMeasure` and `IdentAlg`) were updated; `scripts/comparator-verify.sh` has not been rerun since.
Not yet formalized: the remaining prerequisites of Part II of the blueprint (continuity/attainment of the width, the sub-Gaussian generality of Median Elimination, Gaussian quadratic forms, the sequential composition lemma `lem:composition`, which is no longer used, and the standalone fixed-design algorithm of `lem:ball_identification`, whose two estimates are formalized as the second phase of the block algorithm).

readme.text:
# Formalization of "On the Power of Adaptivity for ε-Best Arm Identification in Linear Bandits" (Maiti, Xu, Jamieson, COLT 2026)

A Lean 4 formalization, built on Mathlib and the [Lean Machine Learning](https://github.com/LeanMachineLearning/LML) library (LML), of the minimax sample-complexity results of the paper: the non-adaptive fixed-design upper bound in terms of a Gaussian width of the action set, the matching lower bounds, the structured action sets on which adaptivity only gives logarithmic gains, the $\ell_2$-norm estimation procedure and the action set on which adaptivity gives a polynomial improvement.

The development is blueprint-driven: `blueprint/src/` contains a detailed proof document (a [leanblueprint](https://github.com/PatrickMassot/leanblueprint)) that decomposes the paper into lemmas whose proofs go from what Mathlib/LML already provide to the paper's results. Part II of the blueprint collects the prerequisites that are meant to be contributed upstream (Gaussian concentration, sub-exponential variables, divergence decompositions of algorithm-environment sequences, Median Elimination, ...).

* Paper source: `source/`
* Blueprint: `blueprint/src/` (build with `leanblueprint pdf` / `leanblueprint web` from `blueprint/`)
* Lean library: `Maiti2026Power/`
* Blueprint outline, design decisions and upstreaming candidates: `notes/`

## Status and layout

The formalization proceeds in two phases. **Phase 1 (done)** states the headline results of the paper in Lean — Theorems 1–3, 5–8, Proposition 4 and the adaptive lower bounds of Table 1 — as `sorry`-ed theorems over definitions written in library generality; they are listed in `formalization.yaml` and each has a self-contained [comparator](https://github.com/leanprover/comparator) challenge file in `comparator/` (see `comparator/README.md`). **Phase 2** proves them, following the blueprint: all of them are now proved (Theorems 1–3, 5–8, Proposition 4 and the five lower bounds of Table 1), with no `sorry` left in the repository, and every challenge is verified by comparator (`scripts/comparator-verify.sh`, all 17 configs pass) (see the `status` section of `formalization.yaml`).

* `Maiti2026Power/LeanMachineLearning/`: material for LML, on top of LML's identification algorithms (`Learning.IdentAlg`: sampling rule, stopping rule, output rule; their runs on a probability space in the LML `IsAlgEnvSeq` framework and PAC guarantees) — fixed budgets and fixed designs (`IdentAlg.lean`), the canonical run of any identification algorithm (`Run.lean`); the linear Gaussian bandit, simple regret and `(ε, δ)`-PAC identification (`LinearBandit.lean`).
* `Maiti2026Power/Mathlib/`: material for Mathlib — the Gaussian width of a set for a measure, measurability on sigma types.
* `Maiti2026Power/MXJ2026/`: the paper — design matrices and the Gaussian width term (`Width.lean`), the structured action sets (`StructuredSets.lean`), and one file per result (`Upper`, `LowerAdaptive`, `LowerNonadaptive`, `WidthBounds`, `LogGains`, `Separation`, `NormEstimation`).
* `comparator/`: challenge files and configs, generated by `scripts/make-challenges.py`; `scripts/comparator-verify.sh` runs comparator.
